notes.1a: Most candidates took a correct set of readings.
notes.1bi: (ii) Most candidates took a correct set of readings and added the correct units to the table. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics November 2021 (c) Many candidates gained partial credit, but some did not make clear reference to the values in their results.
notes.1di: (ii) Most candidates successfully carried out both calculations, but a few did not give the correct unit.
notes.1ei: Many candidates gave imprecise answers with confusing responses about which beaker they were referring to. Several candidates described repeating the experiment with a lid. This was an example where careful reading of the question was needed.
notes.1eii: Most candidates gained partial credit for stating that the starting temperature must be the same with many gaining full credit for correctly explaining that the cooling rate was different at different temperatures.
notes.2a: Many candidates successfully recorded the result for 90 cm of wire A and calculated R.
notes.2bi: Many candidates correctly completed the table but a few did not record their results to the consistency of either 2 or 3 significant figures that was required.
notes.2bii: Most candidates correctly identified all the units needed.
notes.2ci: (ii) Most candidates correctly calculated the values of P and Q from their results.
notes.2ciii: There were many correct statements with the justification of being within the limits of experimental accuracy frequently seen.
notes.2d: Only stronger candidates gained credit with others giving answers referring to human error which was not what was asked.
notes.3a: Most candidates successfully completed the table.
notes.3b: Most candidates calculated the values of 1/h I correctly.
notes.3c: Nearly all candidates attempted the graph with most labelling the axes correctly and using suitable scales. The plotting of points was generally very good but some candidates’ points were too large. They should be no larger than half of a small square on the graph. There were many good lines of best fit with an even distribution of points on either side if necessary. Lines should not automatically be extended to the origin.
notes.3di: Many candidates correctly read u o from their graph and were within range.
notes.3dii: Many candidates correctly drew the triangle on the graph to identify how they would calculate the gradient.
notes.3diii: Many candidates correctly calculated the focal length but some were out of range.
notes.3e: The most common correct answers for a difficulty were either putting something (e.g. a ruler) in the way of the light or the image having blurred edges. Using a larger object or marking the image on the screen were the most common improvements to make.
